clock_assumption: 100 MHz wrapper source assumption only; no clock constraint or timing proof
oracle_scope: Manual interface/state expectations derived from the written finite-state rules. They are not logical equivalence, simulation, synthesis, timing, electrical, ADC, calibration, or board results.
global_invariants: Only one master transaction may be in flight; host and safety in-flight ownership are mutually exclusive.
host_result and safety_result are fixed held slots; nothing is evicted or overwritten.
A full host slot blocks a new host request but never blocks the safety fallback command.
Any master result with the wrong tag or no recorded owner is a sticky fault; it is never stored as success.
No vector proves analog gain, ADC value, settling, CS/register state, 16-edge electrical behavior, or a physical safety property.

stimulus: Assume held slots and an active master transaction from a prior run, then hold rst=1 for at least one clk edge.
Set arm=1 while rst is held, then deassert rst with arm still high.
expected: rst is applied to the 76 master and master_cancel is asserted by the wrapper.
After reset edges, spi_cs_n is high, spi_sck and spi_si are low, both result valid bits are 0, both slots/tags are cleared, armed=0, inhibit=0, sticky_fault=0, and no post-reset ACK appears.
Because arm_q observed the held arm level during reset, the post-reset held-high arm is not a new rising pulse; the wrapper remains unarmed.
Host software must retain its own persistent UNKNOWN state for the destroyed transaction.
vectors.not_proven: No claim that the interrupted analog state is known or restored.

stimulus: From reset, set enable=1, arm=0, cancel=0, overrange=0.
Hold host_valid=1 with tagA and gain4 for many cycles.
expected: armed remains 0 and host_ready remains 0.
No master command is issued and no SPI transaction starts.
Both result slots remain empty.
vectors.not_proven: No inference that an external integrator will default enable low; that is an integration requirement.

stimulus: Pulse arm while cancel=1.
Pulse arm while overrange=1.
Pulse arm while either result slot is full.
Pulse arm while the 76 master is in its post-reset/high-guard state with m_cmd_ready=0.
expected: Each pulse is ignored: armed stays 0 and no command qualification opens.
overrange latches inhibit even when arm is ignored.
A new rising arm pulse is required after all preconditions later become true.
vectors.not_proven: No exact edge count or timing is claimed for the master guard.

stimulus: With empty slots, overrange=0, master ready, and host_valid=1 held from before the arm cycle, pulse arm.
Keep host_valid=1 for many cycles, then drive host_valid=0 for one cycle, then assert host_valid with tagA/gain4.
expected: The arm pulse can set armed=1 and clear inhibit, but host_gate remains 0 because no post-arm host_valid=0 has been observed.
host_ready remains 0 and the old held host_valid cannot handshake or replay.
Only the later host_valid=0 cycle opens host_gate; the subsequent fresh host_valid assertion can handshake if all other gates are eligible.
vectors.not_proven: No exhaustive proof of all upstream valid/ready protocol violations.

vectors.focus: normal host transfer and held result
stimulus: Arm safely, observe host_valid=0, then assert host_valid=1, host_tag=tagA, host_gain_code=gain4.
Hold host_result_ready=0 after the result appears.
expected: host_valid && host_ready transfers exactly one request and records tagA as the host in-flight owner.
The wrapper presents gain4 and tagA to the unchanged 76 master; the wrapper adds no encoder.
On the master's digital terminal result, host_result_valid becomes 1 with error=0 and tag=tagA; safety_result_valid remains 0.
The host result remains held and unchanged while host_result_ready=0, and no new host request is accepted.
vectors.not_proven: error=0 is digital frame completion only; no analog gain or ADC measurement is proven.

stimulus: After safe arm, assert host_valid=1, host_tag=tagA, host_gain_code=3'd3.
expected: The wrapper performs the tag check and may hand the transfer to the 76 master.
The 76 master, not the wrapper, refuses the illegal gain and returns its held digital error with tagA.
host_result_valid=1, host_result_error=1, host_result_tag=tagA; no wrapper success or analog claim is made.
vectors.not_proven: The wrapper does not independently re-encode or establish an SPI waveform for illegal gains.

stimulus: After safe arm and host_gate opening, assert host_valid=1 with host_tag=0 and any gain.
expected: host_ready=0 and no master command is issued.
sticky_fault becomes 1 and inhibit becomes 1; armed is cleared and host_gate closes.
No result is fabricated and the condition persists until reset.
vectors.not_proven: Reset does not repair the lost external transaction context.

stimulus: Arm with reserved_safety_tag=tagS, observe host_valid=0, then assert host_valid=1 with host_tag=tagS.
expected: host_ready=0 because the host tag equals the latched safety tag.
sticky_fault=1, inhibit=1, armed=0, host_gate=0; no master command and no fallback identity is fabricated.
No host or safety result slot is written by the rejected attempt.
vectors.not_proven: No claim that an upstream host cannot violate the tag contract.

stimulus: Complete a normal host transaction so host_result_valid=1 with tagA.
Hold host_result_ready=0 and assert host_valid=1 with tagB.
After one or more cycles, pulse host_result_ready=1 while host_valid may remain high.
expected: While the host slot is full, host_ready remains 0 and no new host command is accepted.
The held host error/tag payload stays stable and is never overwritten.
After the host result-ready edge clears the slot, a still-asserted valid may handshake on the next eligible cycle; this is normal backpressure, not replay of the armed pre-arm request.
vectors.not_proven: No unbounded queue or bypass is provided.

stimulus: Arm safely and open host_gate, then drive overrange=1 in the same cycle as host_valid=1 with tagA/gain4.
Keep overrange high after the edge.
expected: host_ready is 0 in that cycle because the combinational host path includes !overrange; no host handshake occurs.
inhibit becomes 1 at the edge and fallback becomes pending for the safety owner.
No host result is created for the blocked attempt; the fallback gain0 command can be sent only after the 76 master is ready.
vectors.not_proven: No threshold, ADC sample, or calibration source is modeled.

stimulus: Accept host tagA mid-frame, then assert overrange=1 before the normal digital terminal result.
Keep the host result slot empty and do not consume the host result.
expected: master_cancel is asserted for the in-flight host owner while overrange/inhibit applies.
The 76 master returns its digital terminal/error result with tagA; the wrapper stores it in the host slot, sets host_inflight=0, and drains that master result.
The host result slot holds tagA/error and is not overwritten by fallback.
After the original result is drained and the master is ready, exactly one gain0 safety command is issued with tagS; its result goes only to the safety slot.
vectors.not_proven: An abort may already have affected analog state; the eventual gain remains unknown and no CS/register success is inferred.

stimulus: Leave a normal host result tagA held in the host slot with host_result_ready=0.
With no host transaction in flight, assert overrange=1 and keep the host slot full.
expected: inhibit latches and fallback becomes pending without waiting for host_result_ready.
Once the 76 master is ready, the safety tagS/gain0 command is issued even though the host slot is full.
The safety result is stored only in safety_result_valid/error/tag while the host tagA payload remains byte-for-byte stable.
No host slot overwrite or eviction occurs.
vectors.not_proven: This does not prove analog recovery or an ADC overrange threshold.

stimulus: After V11 or V12 has issued fallback and stored its safety result, hold overrange=1 for many cycles with both slots held.
Toggle unrelated host controls while the safety tag remains valid.
expected: No additional gain0 command is issued and fallback_pending remains 0.
No new safety result replaces the held one; no host request is admitted while inhibit is high.
The original host/safety result slots remain stable.
vectors.not_proven: No claim about repeated real ADC events beyond the provided overrange input.

stimulus: After an overrange episode, drive overrange=0 and drain both result slots.
Do not pulse arm.
expected: inhibit remains 1, armed remains 0, and host_ready remains 0.
No automatic host replay, fallback retry, or command qualification occurs.
vectors.not_proven: Low overrange is not itself evidence that the analog input is safe.

stimulus: After overrange is low, leave one result slot full and pulse arm.
Then consume the remaining result and issue a new rising arm pulse while overrange=0 and the master is idle.
expected: The first arm pulse is ignored; inhibit stays 1 and armed stays 0.
The later valid pulse sets armed=1, clears inhibit, clears fallback state, and keeps host_gate=0 until a post-arm host_valid=0 cycle is observed.
No old host request is restarted.
vectors.not_proven: Explicit arm is an external operator/controller action and is not validated as a human safety authorization.

stimulus: With no overrange, accept host tagA mid-frame, then assert cancel=1 for one or more cycles.
Deassert cancel while keeping enable=1.
expected: master_cancel is asserted and the 76 master returns a digital error terminal for tagA when the operation is active.
The wrapper stores tagA/error in the host slot and clears host_inflight; no safety fallback is pending solely because of cancel.
armed is cleared, enable recovery does not auto-arm, and the held result remains until consumed.
vectors.not_proven: Cancel does not guarantee analog state or eliminate a partial-frame effect.

stimulus: Issue fallback tagS/gain0, then assert enable=0 (or cancel) while the safety transaction is active.
Return enable=1 and leave overrange low, but do not pulse arm.
expected: master_cancel is asserted; the 76 master returns its digital terminal/error for tagS.
The wrapper stores the safety result with tagS and error, clears safety in-flight, and performs no automatic retry.
inhibit remains 1, armed remains 0, and host_ready remains 0 until slots are drained and a new explicit safe arm occurs.
vectors.not_proven: A failed fallback is not converted to success and its analog effect is unknown.

vectors.focus: no replay of pending safety request
stimulus: Overrange latches while a host result slot is held and the master is temporarily not ready, so fallback is pending but not yet sent.
Assert cancel before m_cmd_ready becomes 1, then deassert cancel and hold enable=1 without a new arm pulse.
expected: fallback_pending is cleared on cancel; no safety command is sent after cancel deasserts.
inhibit remains 1 and armed remains 0.
A later explicit arm is required after overrange is low and both slots are drained; the dropped fallback is not automatically retried.
vectors.not_proven: This records a conservative unfulfilled fallback behavior, not a safety-complete product.

stimulus: Accept host tagA, then force the observed master result_valid=1 with tagB (or another tag unequal to tagA).
expected: No host or safety result slot is written and master_result_ready is not asserted by the wrapper.
sticky_fault=1 and inhibit=1; armed is cleared and all command admission closes.
The mismatch is not converted into a digital or analog success, and the master result remains an explicit fault witness.
vectors.not_proven: A forced tag mismatch is an interface fault; no claim is made about the real device's tag generation.

stimulus: With no host or safety transaction in flight, force master result_valid=1 with any tag.
expected: sticky_fault=1, inhibit=1, armed=0; no result is accepted or stored.
No fallback or host command is issued while faulted.
vectors.not_proven: No protocol recovery is implemented.

stimulus: From reset with overrange=0, empty slots, and master ready, pulse arm while reserved_safety_tag=0.
expected: The arm is refused; sticky_fault=1 and inhibit=1, armed=0 and host_gate=0.
No host or safety command can start; production integration remains disabled until a distinct nonzero reserved tag is supplied and reset/recovery is separately reviewed.
vectors.not_proven: No legal reserved tag has been assigned by the product/protocol owner; this is a documented blocker.

stimulus: Arm with tagS latched, then change reserved_safety_tag to tagC before any overrange or host handshake.
expected: The next clk edge raises sticky_fault and inhibit; armed is cleared and host_ready is 0.
No fallback with the changed or old identity is started after the fault.
vectors.not_proven: The input is expected to be static by contract; no dynamic reconfiguration protocol is defined.

stimulus: Hold a host result tagA in its slot and trigger fallback while the host slot remains full; allow the safety result tagS to complete.
Keep both result_ready inputs low for many cycles.
expected: Both valid bits are 1 simultaneously; host payload remains tagA and safety payload remains tagS.
No queue growth, eviction, or cross-slot overwrite occurs.
Each slot clears only with its own valid && ready handshake.
vectors.not_proven: No throughput or timing closure claim is made.

stimulus: Start a host transaction or safety fallback, then assert rst=1 while it is active; deassert rst afterward.
expected: master_cancel and master reset force safe SPI outputs; the master destroys its active result/context.
Wrapper in-flight bits and both slots are cleared; no result and no ACK is produced for the interrupted owner.
Post-reset armed=0 and host_ready=0; external host must preserve UNKNOWN and must not reuse the old action.
vectors.not_proven: Reset does not restore the PGA to a measured gain and does not prove physical safety.

stimulus: Leave a result valid in one slot, then pulse arm in a cycle where its ready is also asserted, so the slot is empty only after the edge.
expected: arm_space_ok observes the pre-edge full slot and ignores the arm pulse; inhibit stays 1 and armed stays 0.
After the slot clears, a new rising arm pulse is required; the consumed pulse is not retried automatically.
vectors.not_proven: No automatic re-arm policy is provided.

stimulus: Trigger one fallback with tagS/gain0 and observe either a normal 76 digital completion or its error/cancel terminal.
Consume the safety result through safety_result_valid && safety_result_ready.
expected: error=0 means only digital frame completion; error=1 means refused or aborted.
Inhibit remains set after the result is consumed; no host request is admitted without a new safe arm.
No result is labeled as measured gain, ADC value, settled output, or physical safety success.
vectors.not_proven: R04 ADC/calibration/5%/8-level/settling evidence remains absent.

blocked_or_missing: No legal reserved_safety_tag has been assigned by the product/protocol owner.
No real ADC overrange flag, threshold, calibration, input fixture, or settling model exists.
No pin mapping, level shifting, isolation, clock constraint, timing closure, synthesis, implementation, or board evidence exists.
No H12, 100 MHz timing, final 1%/100 ms target, all-29-card, or overall H01-H15 acceptance is claimed.
